title: A, an, the or nothing?
tagline: A, an, the or nothing: choosing the right article (or none at all).
why: Articles are tiny words, but they're everywhere: a pencil, the sun, no article before football or breakfast. Getting them right is one of the hardest things for Spanish speakers, and the exam checks it constantly in Reading Parts 5 and 6.

hook.text: It's Friday. Miss Vega asks about the weekend. "I'm going to the cinema," says Sofia. "I'm playing football," says Mateo. "I want to read a book about an astronaut," says Nadia.
hook.ask: Some words have a or an, some have the, and some have no article at all. Can you spot all three types in the story?

diagrams.title: How to choose a or an

steps.label: Listen to the sound of the next word, not the letter

diagrams.caption: It's the sound that matters, not the spelling: a university (sounds like 'y'), an hour (silent h).

use.point: a/an: one of many, or a job

examples.text: I need a pencil for the test.

examples.note: the first time you mention something

use.point: the: something specific, known or unique

examples.text: I saw a dog in the park. The dog was brown.
examples.note: the second time you mention it, it's specific

use.point: No article: meals, sports, languages, general plurals

examples.note: meals in general take no article
sports in general take no article
general plural nouns take no article

use.point: Fixed expressions: go to school/bed, at home, the cinema

examples.note: no article for the activity of school

examples.text: On Saturday we went to the cinema and then to the beach.

watch_out.why: Jobs always need a or an in English.

watch_out.wrong: The football is my favourite sport.
watch_out.why: Sports in general take no article.

watch_out.wrong: I go to the school every day.
watch_out.why: The activity of studying takes no article.

watch_out.wrong: We had the lunch at one o'clock.
watch_out.why: Meals take no article when you talk about them in general.
Unique things like the sun, the moon and the sky always need the.

l1.why: Spanish drops the article with jobs, but English never does.
Spanish uses el with sports in general; English uses no article.

l1.wrong: I go to the school by bus.
l1.why: Talking about the activity of studying, English drops the — not just the preposition.
English never drops the article before a unique thing like the sun.

remember.trick: A/an = one of many. THE = we both know it!
remember.tip: Ask yourself: is this just ONE OF MANY things (a/an), or do we BOTH already know which one (the)?

can_do: I can use a and an for one of many things and for jobs.
I can use the for something specific, known or unique.
I can leave out the article with meals, sports, languages and places like school and home.
summary: Use a/an for one of many things, and always with jobs: a teacher, an engineer.
Use the for something specific, known, unique or mentioned before: the sun, the book on the table.
Meals, sports, languages and general plurals take no article: breakfast, football, Spanish, cats.
Some places are fixed expressions: go to school/bed/work, at home, but real places need the: the cinema, the beach.
